claims.text: The starting material is an as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi melt-spun microribbon.
The as-deposited ribbon has a uniform, ordered hexagonal phase.
A spatially nonuniform annealing history can generate a gradient in chemical order, texture, or phase constitution.
The proposed annealing treatment will produce a surface-to-core gradient rather than merely a uniform microstructural change.
The induced order and texture gradient will create spatial variation in magnetostructural transformation temperatures.
The induced gradient will create spatial variation in nucleation kinetics for the magnetostructural transition.
Regions with different local transformation temperatures will transform sequentially as a cascade rather than in one abrupt collective event.
A cascade of local transformations will broaden and smooth the temperature-dependent magnetocaloric entropy-change response.
The distributed transformation will reduce energy-barrier variations that contribute to hysteresis.
Gradient annealing will reduce magnetic and thermal hysteresis relative to the as-deposited homogeneous ribbon.
The broadened response and lower hysteresis can be obtained while retaining a significant entropy change.
The as-deposited homogeneous ribbon exhibits a sharp first-order magnetostructural transition with a large but hysteretic entropy change.
The predicted effect requires a sufficiently broad gradient to produce meaningful variation in local transformation kinetics.
A shallow gradient will diminish the predicted broadening and hysteresis reduction.
Overannealing may change the desired phase instead of producing a controlled order-disorder gradient.
Gradient annealing is to be performed over approximately 300–700 °C for 1–5 minutes under an inert atmosphere.
The magnetocaloric and hysteresis tests are to use cycling applied magnetic fields below 1 T.
Failure to observe both transition broadening and reduced hysteresis relative to the uniform-annealed control would falsify the proposed gradient-mediated explanation.
